thread.title: Apple Down, Fights To Keep This Key Level | Investor's Business Daily

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Apple Down, Fights To Keep This Key Level | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple suffered a second straight heavy sell-off, yet the Wall Street darling is failing to turn the Dow Jones industrial average or the S&P 500 lower. But stocks today are certainly showing mixed action ahead of a highly touted U.S. midterm election.
X Meanwhile, a better than expected print on the ISM services sector survey seemed to keep institutional investors focused on leaders in the consumer and health care sectors. Ulta Beauty ( ULTA ), for instance, is close to a new breakout. Shares in the cosmetics, hair and skin care retailer rallied 1.1%.
Ulta Beauty is currently one of four stocks that hold a "Leaders near a buy point" position within IBD Leaderboard . On IBD Stock Checkup , the large-cap consumer play gets a maximum 99 Composite Rating on a scale of 1 to 99.
The Institute for Supply Management's non-manufacturing index rose to 60.3 in October, beating the Econoday forecast of 59.1. It's a slight drop from a 61.6 reading in September, yet still shows expansionary activity. A 50 reading is considered neutral.
At 2 p.m. ET, the Nasdaq, weighed by a more than 3% sell-off in Apple ( AAPL ) and a 3% drubbing of Google owner Alphabet ( GOOGL ), slumped nearly 1%. The decline follows a nearly 2.7% rebound by the composite index last week.
While the Nasdaq stands roughly 10% below an all-time peak of 7133, Alphabet has stooped more than 19% below its peak of 1,291.
The Dow Jones industrials, however, edged 0.5% higher on the strength of energy, health care and financial components. The S&P 500 rose 0.2%.
The Dow utility average gained 1.1%. At 733, the sector index is up 1.4% year to date.
Homebuilding, tobacco, department store integrated and international oil and gas, steel, solar and ethical drug makers paced the upside. So did heavy construction, packaged food, property REIT and coal shares. All 12 industry groups rallied 1.5% or more.
What To Do With Apple Now Apple dived as much as 4.5% and hit a session low of 198.17 before recouping a bit of the day's bitter losses. Volume is running more than double its 50-day average. The stock's Accumulation/Distribution Rating has fallen to a D+ on a scale of A (huge net buying by funds) to E (huge net selling).
Shares have now given back most of the solid 20% gain after Apple cleared a superb flat base with a 194.30 proper buy point initially on July 25.
Last week the iPhone, iPad, MacBook and Apple Watch marketer gave a damp forecast for sales in the current holiday quarter. Yet the megacap tech still rides a path of solid profit growth. The Street expects fiscal first-quarter earnings to climb 24% to $4.81 a share, on top of a 16% increase in the year-ago quarter.
Those who have a serious profit cushion can afford to see if the stock can bounce back, form a new base , and attempt a fresh breakout.
But recent buyers need to keep their losses small at 7% to 8% or less .
Analysts see sales rising just 5% to $92.62 billion in fiscal Q1. That would represent a sharp deceleration from year-over-year increases of 12%, 13%, 16%, 17% and 20% in the prior five quarters.
The Nasdaq 100 is off nearly 1.1%. The Russell 2000 slipped nearly 0.6%.
This Health Care Play Rises A 3rd Day In A Row Among new IPOs, retail chain National Vision ( EYE ) rallied more than 1% to 43.89 and jumped back above the 50-day moving average, a bullish sign.
The specialist in eyeglasses and eye exams is featured in The New America weekly feature. The stock is forming the right side of a cup base. The cup's left-side high is 46.63. National Vision currently trades roughly 5% below that peak.
National Vision is expected to post a 50% jump in third-quarter earnings to 12 cents a share. In Q2, profit soared 133% to 21 cents a share on a 14% lift in sales to $385.5 million.
In the telecom gear sector, Ciena ( CIEN ) blasted sharply higher, rising as high as 5.3% in intense turnover.
The specialist in fiber optic data networking equipment is clearing a nine-week flat base with a prime buy point of 32.43. The 5% buy zone goes up to 34.05.
Ciena joined IBD Swing Trader earlier in the day.
In Other Financial Markets Crude oil edged higher after selling off hard in recent weeks. A ban on Iranian oil exports from the U.S. and its trading partners has ironically led to a swift correction in crude prices. WTI near-term futures rose 0.3% to $63.32 a barrel.
The yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasury note fell 3 basis points to 3.19%. The yield is still up sharply from a 2.46% reading on Jan. 1.
